## What's new

**Connect to a server without leaving the app.** `Cmd+K`, the new plug button in
the path bar, or File ▸ **Connect to Server…**. Choose NFS or Windows (SMB), type
the address (`192.168.100.100/share`, `nas.local`, `host:/export`), and add a
username and password for SMB. The sheet builds the URL, so nobody types
`smb://user:pass@host/share` by hand. Both protocols mount directly — no Finder
window, no detour through the sidebar.

**Mounted volumes in the sidebar.** Shares, disk images and external disks get a
**Volumes** section. Right-click one to eject it. Ejecting the folder you are in
leaves you in the nearest folder that still exists instead of an empty list.

**Recent servers.** The last 20 addresses that connected, newest first. A
dropdown arrow on the address field shows them, and typing filters them. Picking
one fills the address and the username, so only the password is left — the
password itself is never stored.

**The last row is reachable again.** In a folder with enough links — or while
showing search results — the list could stop short and leave the last row behind
the status bar, unreachable. The table now takes its height from the rows it
actually draws, so every row can be scrolled to.

## Installing

Download `RoachExplorer-v0.1.5.zip`, unzip it, and drag **Roach Explorer** into
Applications. The app is ad-hoc signed, so the first launch may need
right-click → Open. Verify the download with the SHA-256 file next to it:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c RoachExplorer-v0.1.5.zip.sha256
```

Requires macOS 14 or later.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/HenzeLars/RoachExplorer/compare/v0.1.4...v0.1.5
